commandRoutes.provenanceRule: provenance names every slot exactly once. A value whose provenance the case states (formerly embedded in the slot value or a per-slot valueProvenance map) keeps it. grantAuthorization.rule: User decision 2026-10-09 (AGENTS.md): a grant naming several dimension kinds authorizes only when every kind matches the targets the product presents (all-of, IdentityAuthorization.permittedScopes); identifiers within one kind are alternatives, and the policy guard requires every presented identifier of a command (PolicyCommandGuard.everyScope). The fixture schema and the Step 3 installer hold one grant per actor, so a fixture grant keeps only the dimension kinds that every capability the cases call with that actor presents (directly or through it as a fixture delegator): ITEM when all those capabilities carry the item (familiesWithoutItem name those that do not, and an OBJECT read of a noun without item counts the same), none otherwise (an organization-wide grant). WORK, PLACE, TARGET and SOURCE restrictions of a multi-purpose grant would refuse its own reads (an inventory or item row presents no WORK; a Work presents no PLACE), so conform_fixture drops them unless an override keeps them for a negative oracle. Keys with no product grant scope kind are dropped too: the installer could not install them. check_request_contracts.py then proves statically, per subcase, that every read or command the case expects to be authorized is covered and that every action pinned to FORBIDDEN stays uncovered.

requiredFill.description: Required slots the shared-slot cases (declaredOnlyCases) did not state (step2r round 13, run-7b6c69b4: 35 negative authorization probes answered TYPE_INVALID before the authorization they test). Plan section 3.3 validates required slots, type, unit and cardinality before the applicable policy, so a probe that must reach the authorization check sends a type-valid complete request. Each missing required slot takes the first available source: a slot of the same request, a typed subject (@Type), a fixture alias that exists (@alias:NAME), a fixture prior fact (@fact:ALIAS.field), the fixture document named by the first request evidenceRefs entry (@document:path|mediaType|sha256|base64), the typed evidence subject of the one subjectRef (@evidenceSubject), the item of the QuantitySegment subject (@subjectItem), the requesting actor's granted item (@actorItem, @actorItemScopes), the unit of the quantity slot (@quantityUnit), the fixture clock settings (@fixture:timezone|precision), the product clock at the action (@clock, @clock+ISO-8601 duration), the first request evidenceRefs entry (@evidenceRefs), a SHA-256 of a fixed text (@sha256:text) or a literal (@literal:json). Values the requester sets are USER, values taken from the fixture or the clock are CONTEXT. Slots that need an entity the fixture does not install (stocktake, receipt, canonical occurrence, cargo, leg, investigation, outbox) stay KNOWN_OPEN S2-SLOT-REQUIRED until the installer writes those aliases.
